verdict.rationale: Unit's API reference is explicitly a static Docusaurus render with example requests and no in-page runner, so the reference itself is not interactive. Unit does publish its own Postman collection, preset to the Sandbox, which lets users run requests immediately, and an OpenAPI 3.0 spec backs it. Runnable examples therefore exist, but only through an external tool. Missing for 10: an interactive in-page API explorer/try-it console, runnable examples embedded in the reference, and independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can explore an interactive API reference with runnable examples

citations.quote: The hosted Postman v2.1 collection ("Unit API") is the vendor's documented request-trying surface; the API reference itself is a static Docusaurus render with example requests and no in-page runner.
You can interact immediately with the Unit API via Postman
Unit's Sandbox environment is a full replica of the production environment — all standard API endpoints work exactly the same way.
